name: Alabama
overview: In Alabama each county's tax collecting official (the revenue commissioner or tax collector) decides how to collect delinquent property taxes: by selling the property itself at a public tax sale, or by selling the county's tax liens at a public auction. Under the tax-sale method, the Alabama Department of Revenue says a public tax auction is held every year, usually around the first Monday in May, and the owner may redeem within 3 years of the sale by paying the taxes, fees and interest at 12% per annum. Under the tax-lien method, the official auctions delinquent tax liens, the certificate earns the interest rate the buyer bid at the auction, and the holder may not file to foreclose until three years after the auction.

counties.schedule_rule: First Week of May each year-Tax Lien Sale & Auction-Online Only.
counties.how_to_bid: Online-only tax lien auction on GovEase. Registration opens 30 days before the auction and applications are made through GovEase. Bids run from a 12% maximum down to 0% (simple interest per annum, prorated monthly). Payment in full by cash, certified funds or wire is due at least one hour before the end of sale day; credit cards are not accepted. Interest stops on the day of redemption, and a lien expires if foreclosure is not started within ten years.

counties.how_to_bid: Online tax lien auction on GovEase; register on GovEase and submit a 10% deposit. Bidding on each lien starts at no more than 12% interest and drops in 1% steps toward 0%; each lien is open 30 seconds, and ties at 0% are broken by a random number generator. Pay GovEase by e-check, ACH or wire no later than one hour before close of business on the final day. Redemptions go through the Revenue Commissioner's office in certified funds, with a $10 redemption fee.
